decisions.reason: Because it is a recently launched plugin close to the core webshop service offer in a growing market and the firm appears to have enough slack from hiring and in-house development to give it more time.

An ERP interface plugin strongly complements the firm's end-to-end ecommerce positioning and multichannel direction, so management would likely retain it unless early results were clearly disappointing.

It fits the established optimization and analytics business, but the presence of several similar price-comparison tracking plugins raises some chance of later consolidation if performance falls short of aspirations.

As a related plugin launched only recently, it would usually be kept for further learning, though overlap with other similar plugins makes pruning somewhat more plausible than for more distinctive products.
The product is close to existing capabilities and the firm has reasons to continue problemistic search within this area, but duplication among similar offerings creates a moderate risk of withdrawal.

This reporting plugin is adjacent to the firm's established technical and analytics services, and in the absence of clear failure a boundedly rational management with some slack would likely continue it for another year.
